lines.k1: Kafka is a distributed log: events are appended and kept, not removed when they are read.
lines.k2: Each consumer tracks its own offset, so many consumers can read the same events at their own pace.
lines.k3: A topic is split into partitions, so writes and reads spread across many machines.
lines.k4: Events with the same key always go to the same partition, so their order is kept.
lines.k5: Partitions are replicated across brokers, so the data survives a machine failure.
lines.k6: Because events are kept, you can replay history: rebuild a service, or feed a new consumer from the start.
lines.k7: Kafka is a great fit for event streaming, analytics pipelines, and event sourcing.
